# Terraform AWS WAFv2 Management Module

 [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management/commits)


Terraform module to manage a single AWS WAFv2 Web ACL with any combination of
AWS Managed Rule Groups, external rule group references, custom rule groups
(created in-module), and custom inline rules supporting all WAFv2 statement
types (byte match, size constraint, SQLi, XSS, regex, IP set, geo match, label
match, rate-based, and compound not/and/or). Supports module-managed IP sets,
regex pattern sets, and API keys with dynamic `ref:` linking into rules.
Includes optional Web ACL associations, automatic CloudWatch Logs group
creation, and centralized logging with field redaction and log filtering.
Designed for both `REGIONAL` (ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner,
Verified Access) and `CLOUDFRONT` scopes.

## Introduction

## Overview

This module provisions and wires together all the resources required for a
production-ready WAFv2 deployment:

| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `aws_wafv2_ip_set` | One per entry in `settings.ip_sets` — module-managed IP allow/block lists |
| `aws_wafv2_regex_pattern_set` | One per entry in `settings.regex_pattern_sets` — module-managed regex libraries |
| `aws_wafv2_api_key` | One per entry in `settings.api_keys` — mobile SDK token domain keys |
| `aws_wafv2_rule_group` | One per entry in `settings.rule_groups` — custom rule groups created and managed by this module |
| `aws_wafv2_web_acl` | Single ACL; rules are attached as standalone `aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule` resources (not inline blocks) |
| `aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule` | One per managed rule, rule group reference, custom rule group reference, or custom inline rule |
| `aws_wafv2_web_acl_association` | One per entry in `settings.associations` — attaches the ACL to ALB, API GW, etc. |
| `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` | Auto-created when `settings.logging.enabled = true`; named `aws-waf-logs-<acl-name>` |
| `aws_wafv2_web_acl_logging_configuration` | Optional logging to Kinesis Firehose, S3, or CloudWatch Logs |

### Design principles

* **Rules are standalone resources, not inline ACL blocks.** Every rule is
  an `aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule` resource attached to the ACL by ARN. The
  `aws_wafv2_web_acl` resource itself contains no inline rule blocks, keeping
  ACL plans clean and diff-free as rules are added or changed.
* **Rule drift is ignored after creation.** The Web ACL has `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [rule] }`,
  so rules changed outside Terraform (e.g. by AWS Firewall Manager or the console)
  are not reverted on subsequent plan/apply runs.
* **`ref:` linking for dynamic ARN resolution.** Use `ref: "<name>"` instead of a
  literal ARN in `ip_set_reference`, `regex_pattern_set_reference`, and
  `rule_group_references[]` to reference resources created within this module.
  Terraform resolves the ARN at plan time with full dependency tracking.
* **Single `settings` variable.** All WAF-specific configuration is passed as a
  structured `any` map, making the module easy to drive from YAML input files in
  a Terragrunt stack.
* **Name or prefix, not both.** Supply either `name` (explicit) or `name_prefix`
  (concatenated with the computed `system_name`) — the module enforces that at
  least one is set.
* **CloudWatch log group is auto-created.** Set `settings.logging.enabled = true`
  and the module creates a `aws-waf-logs-<acl-name>` log group, wires its ARN into
  the logging configuration, and manages retention and KMS encryption.

### `ref` linking — how it works

Instead of a literal `arn`, set `ref: "<name>"` to reference a resource created
by this module. Provide `arn` **or** `ref` — not both. The `name` must match the
`name` field of the target object in `settings`.

| Field | Where | `ref` resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `ip_set_reference.ref` | `rule_groups[].rules[]` and `custom_rules[]` | `settings.ip_sets[name]` ARN |
| `regex_pattern_set_reference.ref` | `rule_groups[].rules[]` and `custom_rules[]` | `settings.regex_pattern_sets[name]` ARN |
| `rule_group_references[].ref` | `rule_group_references[]` | `settings.rule_groups[name]` ARN |

### Supported statement types

**Custom rule groups** (`settings.rule_groups[].rules[]`) support these leaf statements:

| Statement | Key | Supports `ref` |
|---|---|---|
| IP set reference | `ip_set_reference` | yes |
| Geo match | `geo_match` | — |
| Rate-based | `rate_based` | — |
| Byte match | `byte_match` | — |
| Size constraint | `size_constraint` | — |
| Regex pattern set reference | `regex_pattern_set_reference` | yes |

**Custom inline rules** (`settings.custom_rules[]`) support all of the above plus:

| Statement | Key | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Label match | `label_match` | Match by label key or namespace |
| SQL injection match | `sqli_match` | Configurable `sensitivity_level` |
| XSS match | `xss_match` | — |
| Regex match | `regex_match` | Single inline pattern string |
| Regex pattern set reference | `regex_pattern_set_reference` | yes (`ref:`) |
| Not (compound) | `not_statement` | Wraps one leaf statement |
| And (compound) | `and_statement` | Wraps two or more statements |
| Or (compound) | `or_statement` | Wraps two or more statements |

Compound statements support one level of inner nesting (e.g., `and_statement` containing
a `not_statement`). Custom inline rules also support the extended `field_to_match` types
`COOKIES`, `HEADERS`, and `JSON_BODY` (with match pattern and oversize handling) in addition
to the seven core types (`URI_PATH`, `QUERY_STRING`, `METHOD`, `BODY`, `ALL_QUERY_ARGUMENTS`,
`SINGLE_HEADER`, `SINGLE_QUERY_ARGUMENT`).

### Supported AWS Managed Rule Groups (examples)

| Vendor | Name |
|---|---|
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` |
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet` |
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet` |
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesLinuxRuleSet` |
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList` |
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet` *(requires `managed_rule_group_configs`)* |
| AWS | `AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet` *(requires `managed_rule_group_configs`)* |

## Usage


**IMPORTANT:** The `master` branch is used in `source` just as an example. In your code, do not pin to `master` because there may be breaking changes between releases.
Instead pin to the release tag (e.g. `?ref=vX.Y.Z`) of one of our [latest releases](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management/releases).


## Usage (Terragrunt)

### Minimal — managed rules only, explicit name

```hcl
locals {
  local_vars  = yamldecode(file("./inputs.yaml"))
  global_vars = yamldecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-inputs.yaml")))
  global_tags = jsondecode(file(find_in_parent_folders("global-tags.json")))
  local_tags  = jsondecode(file("./local-tags.json"))
  tags        = merge(local.global_tags, local.local_tags)
}

include "root" {
  path = find_in_parent_folders("root.hcl")
}

terraform {
  source = "git::https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management.git//?ref=v1.0.0"
}

inputs = {
  org        = local.global_vars.org
  spoke_def  = local.local_vars.spoke_def
  extra_tags = local.tags

  name = try(local.local_vars.name, null)

  settings = {
    scope          = "REGIONAL"
    default_action = "allow"

    managed_rules = [
      {
        name     = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet"
        priority = 10
      },
      {
        name     = "AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet"
        priority = 20
      },
      {
        name            = "AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList"
        priority        = 30
        override_action = "count"  # monitor only
      },
    ]
  }
}
```

### Full — all features enabled

```hcl
inputs = {
  org        = local.global_vars.org
  spoke_def  = local.local_vars.spoke_def
  extra_tags = local.tags

  # Either name OR name_prefix must be set — not both.
  # name        = "acme-prod-waf"
  name_prefix = "acme"   # resolves to "acme-<system_name>"

  settings = {
    scope          = "REGIONAL"   # REGIONAL | CLOUDFRONT
    default_action = "allow"      # allow | block
    description    = "Production WAF ACL — ACME platform"

    visibility_config = {
      cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
      sampled_requests_enabled   = true
      # metric_name defaults to the ACL name
    }

    # ── AWS Managed Rule Groups ────────────────────────────────────────────
    managed_rules = [
      {
        name            = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet"
        priority        = 10
        override_action = "none"   # enforce; use "count" to monitor
        rule_action_overrides = [
          # Override individual rules instead of the whole group
          { name = "SizeRestrictions_BODY", action = "count" },
        ]
      },
      {
        name     = "AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet"
        priority = 20
      },
      {
        name     = "AWSManagedRulesLinuxRuleSet"
        priority = 30
      },
      {
        name     = "AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList"
        priority = 40
      },
      # Bot Control requires managed_rule_group_configs
      {
        name     = "AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet"
        priority = 50
        managed_rule_group_configs = [
          {
            bot_control = {
              inspection_level       = "COMMON"   # COMMON | TARGETED
              enable_machine_learning = true
            }
          }
        ]
      },
    ]

    # ── IP Sets (created by this module, referenceable via ref:) ─────────────
    ip_sets = [
      {
        name               = "blocked-ips"
        ip_address_version = "IPV4"   # IPV4 | IPV6
        addresses = [
          "203.0.113.0/24",
          "198.51.100.42/32",
        ]
        description = "Known bad IPv4 ranges"
      },
    ]

    # ── Regex Pattern Sets (created by this module, referenceable via ref:) ─
    regex_pattern_sets = [
      {
        name        = "malicious-paths"
        description = "Common attack path patterns"
        patterns = [
          "^/admin/.*",
          "^/wp-.*",
          "^\\.env$",
        ]
      },
    ]

    # ── API Keys (mobile SDK token domain integration) ─────────────────────
    api_keys = [
      {
        name = "mobile-app"
        token_domains = [
          "app.example.com",
          "api.example.com",
        ]
      },
    ]

    # ── Web ACL Associations ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    associations = [
      {
        resource_arn = "arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/abcdef01"
      },
    ]

    # ── External Rule Group References (arn or ref — not both) ───────────
    rule_group_references = [
      # Option A: literal ARN of a pre-existing rule group
      {
        name            = "shared-ip-allowlist"
        priority        = 5
        arn             = "arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:123456789012:regional/rulegroup/shared-ip-allowlist/abcdef01"
        override_action = "none"
      },
      # Option B: ref to a rule group created by this module (settings.rule_groups[name])
      {
        name = "ip-controls-via-ref"
        priority = 65
        ref  = "ip-controls"
      },
    ]

    # ── Custom Rule Groups (created by this module) ────────────────────────
    rule_groups = [
      {
        name          = "ip-controls"
        priority      = 60
        capacity      = 50
        description   = "IP reputation and rate limiting"

        rules = [
          # Block using a module-managed IP set (ref resolves to settings.ip_sets[name=blocked-ips])
          {
            name     = "block-bad-ips"
            priority = 1
            action   = "block"
            ip_set_reference = {
              ref = "blocked-ips"
            }
          },
          # Rate limit per source IP
          {
            name     = "rate-limit-per-ip"
            priority = 2
            action   = "block"
            rate_based = {
              limit                 = 2000    # requests per evaluation_window_sec
              aggregate_key_type    = "IP"    # IP | FORWARDED_IP
              evaluation_window_sec = 300
            }
          },
          # Geo-block specific countries
          {
            name     = "geo-block"
            priority = 3
            action   = "block"
            geo_match = {
              country_codes = ["CN", "RU", "KP"]
            }
          },
        ]
      },

      {
        name        = "http-hygiene"
        priority    = 70
        capacity    = 150
        description = "HTTP header and body hygiene checks"

        rules = [
          # Block requests with a specific User-Agent string
          {
            name     = "block-bad-user-agent"
            priority = 1
            action   = "block"
            byte_match = {
              search_string         = "BadBot/1.0"
              positional_constraint = "CONTAINS"   # EXACTLY | STARTS_WITH | ENDS_WITH | CONTAINS | CONTAINS_WORD
              field_to_match = {
                type = "SINGLE_HEADER"
                name = "user-agent"
              }
              text_transformations = [
                { priority = 0, type = "LOWERCASE" }
              ]
            }
          },
          # Block oversized request bodies
          {
            name     = "block-large-body"
            priority = 2
            action   = "block"
            size_constraint = {
              comparison_operator = "GT"   # EQ | NE | LE | LT | GE | GT
              size                = 8192
              field_to_match = {
                type              = "BODY"
                oversize_handling = "CONTINUE"   # NO_MATCH | MATCH | CONTINUE
              }
              text_transformations = [
                { priority = 0, type = "NONE" }
              ]
            }
          },
          # Block paths matching a module-managed regex pattern set (ref resolves to settings.regex_pattern_sets[name=malicious-paths])
          {
            name     = "block-malicious-paths"
            priority = 3
            action   = "block"
            regex_pattern_set_reference = {
              ref = "malicious-paths"
              field_to_match = {
                type = "URI_PATH"
              }
              text_transformations = [
                { priority = 0, type = "LOWERCASE" }
              ]
            }
          },
        ]
      },
    ]

    # ── Custom Inline Rules ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Inline rules are attached directly to the Web ACL as standalone resources.
    # Every WAFv2 statement type is supported. Use action (not override_action).
    custom_rules = [
      # Block requests from known bad IPs (ref to module-managed ip set)
      {
        name     = "block-bad-ips"
        priority = 75
        action   = "block"
        ip_set_reference = {
          ref = "blocked-ips"
        }
        visibility_config = {
          cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
          metric_name                = "AWS-block-bad-ips"
          sampled_requests_enabled   = true
        }
      },
      # Rate-limit per source IP with label tagging
      {
        name     = "rate-limit-api"
        priority = 80
        action   = "block"
        rate_based = {
          limit                 = 1000
          aggregate_key_type    = "IP"
          evaluation_window_sec = 300
        }
        visibility_config = {
          cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
          metric_name                = "AWS-rate-limit-api"
          sampled_requests_enabled   = true
        }
      },
      # SQLi detection on query string
      {
        name     = "detect-sqli"
        priority = 85
        action   = "block"
        sqli_match = {
          sensitivity_level = "HIGH"
          field_to_match = {
            type = "QUERY_STRING"
          }
          text_transformations = [
            { priority = 0, type = "URL_DECODE" },
            { priority = 1, type = "HTML_ENTITY_DECODE" },
          ]
        }
        visibility_config = {
          cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
          metric_name                = "AWS-detect-sqli"
          sampled_requests_enabled   = true
        }
      },
      # Block requests that carry a specific label (set by a managed rule group)
      {
        name     = "block-labeled-bots"
        priority = 90
        action   = "block"
        label_match = {
          scope = "LABEL"
          key   = "awswaf:managed:aws:bot-control:bot:category:scraping"
        }
        visibility_config = {
          cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
          metric_name                = "AWS-block-labeled-bots"
          sampled_requests_enabled   = true
        }
      },
      # Compound: block requests that are NOT from allowed countries AND contain a bad path
      {
        name     = "compound-geo-path-block"
        priority = 95
        action   = "block"
        and_statement = {
          statements = [
            {
              not_statement = {
                geo_match = {
                  country_codes = ["US", "CA", "GB"]
                }
              }
            },
            {
              regex_pattern_set_reference = {
                ref = "malicious-paths"
                field_to_match = { type = "URI_PATH" }
                text_transformations = [{ priority = 0, type = "LOWERCASE" }]
              }
            },
          ]
        }
        visibility_config = {
          cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
          metric_name                = "AWS-compound-geo-path-block"
          sampled_requests_enabled   = true
        }
      },
    ]

    # ── Logging ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Setting enabled = true creates a CloudWatch log group automatically:
    #   aws-waf-logs-<acl-name>  (retention: retention_in_days, optional KMS)
    logging = {
      enabled           = true
      retention_in_days = 90      # 0 = never expire; see valid values in variables-waf.tf
      # kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:..."   # optional — encrypts the log group
      destination_arns = [
        "arn:aws:firehose:us-east-1:123456789012:deliverystream/aws-waf-logs-acme-prod",
      ]
      # Redact sensitive fields from stored logs
      redacted_fields = [
        { type = "QUERY_STRING" },
        { type = "SINGLE_HEADER", name = "authorization" },
      ]
      # Only store blocked and counted requests (drop allowed traffic logs)
      filter = {
        default_behavior = "DROP"
        filters = [
          {
            behavior    = "KEEP"
            requirement = "MEETS_ANY"
            conditions = [
              { action_condition = "BLOCK" },
              { action_condition = "COUNT" },
            ]
          },
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Quick Start

## Quick start

1. **Initialize** a new Terragrunt layer pointing at this module:

   ```hcl
   terraform {
     source = "git::https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-waf-management.git//?ref=v1.0.0"
   }
   ```

2. **Provide** the required inputs — either `name` or `name_prefix` plus
   `settings.scope`:

   ```hcl
   inputs = {
     org         = local.global_vars.org
     name_prefix = "myapp"
     settings = {
       scope = "REGIONAL"
       managed_rules = [
         { name = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet", priority = 10 },
       ]
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Plan and apply**:

   ```shell
   terragrunt plan
   terragrunt apply
   ```

4. **Associate** the resulting `web_acl_arn` output with your ALB, API Gateway
   stage, or CloudFront distribution.


## Examples

## Common examples

### CloudFront scope (global WAF for a CDN distribution)

When protecting a CloudFront distribution the module must be deployed in
`us-east-1` (the only region that accepts `CLOUDFRONT`-scoped resources) and
the resulting `web_acl_arn` output is passed to the CloudFront distribution.

```hcl
inputs = {
  org  = local.global_vars.org
  name = "acme-cloudfront-waf"

  settings = {
    scope          = "CLOUDFRONT"
    default_action = "allow"

    managed_rules = [
      { name = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet",         priority = 10 },
      { name = "AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet", priority = 20 },
    ]
  }
}
```

### Count mode — non-blocking audit before enforcement

Use `override_action = "count"` on all rule groups to observe what would be
blocked without actually blocking traffic. Flip to `"none"` when confident.

```hcl
managed_rules = [
  {
    name            = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet"
    priority        = 10
    override_action = "count"
  },
  {
    name            = "AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet"
    priority        = 20
    override_action = "count"
  },
]
```

### Attaching the ACL to an ALB (inline association)

Pass the ALB ARN in `settings.associations` and the module creates the
`aws_wafv2_web_acl_association` resource automatically:

```hcl
settings = {
  scope = "REGIONAL"
  associations = [
    { resource_arn = "arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:loadbalancer/app/my-alb/abc123" },
  ]
  managed_rules = [
    { name = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet", priority = 10 },
  ]
}
```

Alternatively, associate from the consuming stack using the module output:

```hcl
resource "aws_wafv2_web_acl_association" "alb" {
  resource_arn = aws_lb.this.arn
  web_acl_arn  = module.waf.web_acl_arn
}
```

### Custom inline rules — block with any WAFv2 statement

`settings.custom_rules` creates standalone `aws_wafv2_web_acl_rule` resources
attached directly to the ACL. Use `action` (not `override_action`) — these are
terminal rules, not rule group references.

```hcl
settings = {
  scope = "REGIONAL"

  custom_rules = [
    # XSS detection on request body
    {
      name     = "detect-xss-body"
      priority = 80
      action   = "block"
      xss_match = {
        field_to_match = {
          type              = "BODY"
          oversize_handling = "NO_MATCH"
        }
        text_transformations = [
          { priority = 0, type = "HTML_ENTITY_DECODE" }
        ]
      }
      visibility_config = {
        cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
        metric_name                = "AWS-detect-xss-body"
        sampled_requests_enabled   = true
      }
    },
    # Compound: rate-limit OR geo-block (either condition triggers)
    {
      name     = "rate-or-geo-block"
      priority = 85
      action   = "block"
      or_statement = {
        statements = [
          {
            rate_based = {
              limit                 = 500
              aggregate_key_type    = "IP"
              evaluation_window_sec = 60
            }
          },
          {
            geo_match = {
              country_codes = ["KP", "IR"]
            }
          },
        ]
      }
      visibility_config = {
        cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true
        metric_name                = "AWS-rate-or-geo-block"
        sampled_requests_enabled   = true
      }
    },
  ]

  managed_rules = [
    { name = "AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet", priority = 10 },
  ]
}
```

### Using module-managed IP sets and regex pattern sets with `ref:`

Define the sets inside `settings` and reference them by name in rule statements
using `ref:<name>` — no need to look up ARNs manually:

```hcl
settings = {
  scope = "REGIONAL"

  ip_sets = [
    {
      name               = "scanners"
      ip_address_version = "IPV4"
      addresses          = ["198.51.100.0/24"]
    },
  ]

  regex_pattern_sets = [
    {
      name     = "bad-paths"
      patterns = ["^/\\.git/.*", "^/wp-admin/.*"]
    },
  ]

  rule_groups = [
    {
      name     = "custom-blocks"
      priority = 50
      capacity = 100
      rules = [
        {
          name             = "block-scanners"
          priority         = 1
          action           = "block"
          ip_set_reference = { ref = "scanners" }
        },
        {
          name     = "block-bad-paths"
          priority = 2
          action   = "block"
          regex_pattern_set_reference = {
            ref            = "bad-paths"
            field_to_match = { type = "URI_PATH" }
            text_transformations = [{ priority = 0, type = "LOWERCASE" }]
          }
        },
      ]
    },
  ]
}
```

## Inputs

| Name | Description | Type | Default | Required |
|------|-------------|------|---------|:--------:|
| <a name="input_extra_tags"></a> [extra\_tags](#input\_extra\_tags) | Extra tags to add to the resources | `map(string)` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_is_hub"></a> [is\_hub](#input\_is\_hub) | Is this a hub or spoke configuration? | `bool` | `false` | no |
| <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name) | Explicit name for the WAF ACL. Required when name\_prefix is not set. | `string` | `null` | no |
| <a name="input_name_prefix"></a> [name\_prefix](#input\_name\_prefix) | Name prefix prepended to system\_name to form the WAF ACL name (<name\_prefix>-<system\_name>). Required when name is not set. | `string` | `null` | no |
| <a name="input_org"></a> [org](#input\_org) | Organization details | <pre>object({<br/>    organization_name = string<br/>    organization_unit = string<br/>    environment_type  = string<br/>    environment_name  = string<br/>  })</pre> | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_settings"></a> [settings](#input\_settings) | WAF module settings — controls ACL scope/default-action, IP sets, regex pattern sets, API keys, associations, AWS managed rules, rule group references, custom rule groups, and logging. | `any` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_spoke_def"></a> [spoke\_def](#input\_spoke\_def) | Spoke ID Number, must be a 3 digit number | `string` | `"001"` | no |
